purpose: Verified peer-reviewed and prepublication source additions used in the live Signal and explicit-reasoning measurement review.

records.citation: He, X., Qiu, B., Deng, Y., Liu, T., Chen, Y., & Zhang, W. (2022). Adaptive assessment of the capacity of cognitive control. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 75(1), 43–52.
key_findings: adaptive scores were highly correlated with original-administration scores
the adaptive version showed high test-retest reliability
fewer than 216 trials and about 20 minutes were required compared with 864 trials and about 86 minutes
source code and data were made available
limitations: small healthy-young-adult sample
does not validate the IQ Mindware browser implementation
does not validate relative-frame or optic-flow variants
assessment study rather than training-transfer study

records.citation: Jaeggi, S. M., Buschkuehl, M., Perrig, W. J., & Meier, B. (2010). The concurrent validity of the N-back task as a working memory measure. Memory, 18(4), 394–412.
key_findings: n-back was useful as an experimental working-memory task
the studied versions were not judged useful as individual-differences working-memory measures partly because of insufficient reliability
higher-load n-back performance related to higher cognitive functions
limitations: task versions differ from WM Coach
does not imply that all n-back implementations have poor reliability
does not validate relational or majority-relation n-back

records.citation: Redick, T. S., & Lindsey, D. R. (2013). Complex span and n-back measures of working memory: A meta-analysis. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 20, 1102–1113.
records.population: 20 studies with 2,178 participants in the main task-comparison literature
key_findings: complex span and n-back were weakly correlated on average
substantial heterogeneity was present
the paradigms should not be used interchangeably as working-memory measures
limitations: low observed correlations include task-specific and measurement-error variance
does not rule out a higher-order latent working-memory factor
does not validate or invalidate the exact WM Coach implementation

records.citation: Ripp, I., Emch, M., Wu, Q., Lizarraga, A., Udale, R., von Bastian, C. C., Koch, K., & Yakushev, I. (2022). Adaptive working memory training does not produce transfer effects in cognition and neuroimaging. Translational Psychiatry, 12, 512.
key_findings: eight weeks of adaptive n-back training produced practice effects
the study found no supported transfer effects across its cognitive and neuroimaging outcomes
limitations: middle-aged healthy sample
specific n-back programme
does not test relational-wrapper or Trident-G transfer protocols
does not validate WM Coach

records.citation: Dai, M., Li, Y., Gan, S., & Du, F. (2019). The reliability of estimating visual working memory capacity. Scientific Reports, 9, 1155.
key_findings: test-retest correlations for K by set size ranged from approximately 0.50 to 0.76
reliability tended to increase with set size
same-time-of-day retesting could improve reliability
limitations: lateralised change-detection task rather than the IQ Mindware task
reliability varied by set size
does not establish binding-training transfer

records.citation: Zhao, C., Vogel, E., & Awh, E. (2023). Change localization: A highly reliable and sensitive measure of capacity in visual working memory. Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics, 85(5), 1681–1694.
records.population: healthy adult samples across multiple experiments
key_findings: change localisation captured strongly overlapping individual-difference variance with change detection
split-half reliability was high and typically around 0.90 or above in the reported experiments
approximately 50–75 trials could achieve strong reliability
localisation offered lower chance performance and greater dynamic range than binary detection
limitations: measures capacity rather than the exact conjunction n-back process
does not validate WM Coach
does not establish training transfer

records.citation: McMaster, J. M. V., Tomić, I., Schneegans, S., & Bays, P. M. (2022). Swap errors in visual working memory are fully explained by cue-feature variability. Cognitive Psychology, 137, 101493.
key_findings: swap errors increased with variability in memory for cue features
changes in swap frequency could be quantitatively predicted from cue-feature recall variability
swap responses need not reflect cue-independent binding failure
limitations: continuous cued-recall tasks differ from the IQ Mindware task
does not rule out other causes in other paradigms
does not establish training transfer

records.citation: Radmard, P., Bays, P. M., & Lengyel, M. (2025). A flexible Bayesian non-parametric mixture model reveals multiple dependencies of swap errors in visual working memory. arXiv:2505.01178.
key_findings: the model recovered multiple dependencies in swap behaviour
the results raise the possibility that prior interpretations of swap errors were incomplete
possible encoding contributions were identified alongside cueing and retrieval accounts
limitations: not peer reviewed
descriptive model rather than intervention evidence
not the exact IQ Mindware task

records.citation: O'Leary, A. P., & Fletcher, W. (2024). Thinking about believing: Can metacognitive reflection encourage belief updating? Journal of Intelligence, 12(5), 47.
key_findings: reflection on counterevidence was associated with belief updating
the additional metacognitive-reflection manipulation provided limited incremental evidence
limitations: single study
not a formal reasoning item-bank validation
not an IQ Mindware training study
does not establish workflow transfer

records.citation: Kim, S. (2024). Natural frequencies improve public understanding of medical test results: An experimental study on various Bayesian inference tasks with multiple scoring methods and non-Bayesian reasoning strategies. Medical Decision Making, 44(8), 890–899.
key_findings: natural-frequency formats improved Bayesian inference relative to conditional-probability formats across multiple problems and scoring approaches
higher-numeracy participants benefited more
participants used multiple non-Bayesian strategies depending on task and format
limitations: representation-format study rather than training-transfer evidence
medical-test scenarios may not generalise to every reasoning domain
does not validate Reasoning Coach

records.citation: Guo, L. (2022). Using metacognitive prompts to enhance self-regulated learning and learning outcomes: A meta-analysis of experimental studies in computer-based learning environments. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 38(3), 811–832.
key_findings: metacognitive prompts improved self-regulated-learning activities with g approximately 0.50
learning outcomes improved with g approximately 0.40
effects varied with feedback, specificity and adaptability
limitations: educational prompting rather than cognitive-capacity training
heterogeneous interventions and outcomes
does not validate a Reasoning Coach calibration profile

records.citation: Swaryandini, G., Graham, J., Griffith, S., et al. (2025). Systematic review and meta-analysis of educational approaches to reduce cognitive biases among students. Nature Human Behaviour, 9, 2510–2538.
records.population: students across 54 randomised controlled trials; 10,941 participants
key_findings: educational interventions produced a small targeted debiasing effect, g = 0.26
some biases were difficult to change
depth and transfer beyond classroom tasks remained uncertain
limitations: all included studies had unclear or high risk of bias
some publication-bias risk
heterogeneous interventions
does not establish real-world decision improvement or validate IQ Mindware
